title: Marcel Breuer, club chair B 3 (“Wassily”)
lede: The first tubular steel armchair for the home: a cubic frame of bent tubes with fabric straps for seat, back, and arms.
summary: Bent steel tube frame with taut dark fabric straps. Marcel Breuer, Bauhaus Dessau, 1925–26.
made: 1926 (second version, per Bauhaus Kooperation); first version 1925

evidence.note: Downloaded and inspected, in the scratchpad only, the Stiftung Bauhaus Dessau photograph on the Bauhaus Kooperation page and a [side view by Sailko](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Marcel_breuer,_poltrona_B_3,_1925,_01.JPG) of the example in the Musée national d’art moderne, Paris.

styles.note: The style summary names tubular steel as a Bauhaus material; this chair made it a domestic furniture type.

context: Bauhaus Kooperation says Breuer, the junior master in charge of the Dessau furniture workshop, designed the chair in 1926 as a showpiece of new living; it was later called “Wassily” after Wassily Kandinsky, and it furnished the Dessau Bauhaus building. [Bauhaus Kooperation](https://bauhauskooperation.de/wissen/das-bauhaus/werke/tischlerei/clubsessel-b-3-2-version/).

The Commons photograph labels the Paris example “B 3, 1925.” [Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Marcel_breuer,_poltrona_B_3,_1925,_01.JPG). MoMA dates its example 1927–1928. [MoMA 2851](https://www.moma.org/collection/works/2851).
observed: The frame is made of thin metal tubes with a worn, dull plating, bent into rectangles with rounded corners.
Seen from the side, the base, arms, and back form overlapping rectangles and one strong diagonal.
Dark fabric straps stretch between the tubes to form the seat, the back, and the arm rests.
Screws and joins in the frame are visible.
The chair is open: the floor and the wall show through it from every side.
interpretation: The chair turns the poster grammar of bars and one diagonal into a structure. Tubular steel and canvas are shown as they are.
borrow: Draw with thin continuous lines and rounded corners only where a material bends.
Let one diagonal cross an otherwise orthogonal frame.

rights.statement: No image is stored. The Commons photograph is CC BY 3.0, but the chair design is still protected; Breuer died in 1981. Bauhaus Kooperation’s photograph is credited to Stiftung Bauhaus Dessau / Kelly Kellerhoff.
